correctness.rationale: The exact surplus is (3+3p-p^2)q+3(p^2+p+1). For p>=7, q>=p+2 and the surplus is <=-p^3+4p^2+12p+9<0. At p=5, positive sum of distinct divisors restricts q to 7 or 11, yielding only 550. At p=3, the proper divisors are {1,2,3,6,9,18} union q{1,2,3,6,9}; for q>=17 neither two low, one low and one q-multiple, nor two q-multiple divisors can sum to 3q+39. The q=13 case is excluded by no distinct coefficients in {1,2,3,6,9} summing to 6. Direct complete proper-divisor checks of all remaining cases give precisely 90,126,198,550 and their unique pairs. Independent divisor algorithms and a 4371-prime-pair numerical stress test checked the finite premises, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact 2p^2q classification is not a consequence of earlier theorems restricted to two prime supports or the squarefree 2pq three-prime slice; the 2025 paper explicitly asks for multi-prime family classifications and gives examples rather than unbounded exhaustiveness. A341475 records examples but is not a proof that no larger such examples exist. Accessible research-record and prior-claim searches found no covering theorem. Bibliographic uniqueness is not certified.

value.rationale: The exact first squareful extension 2p^2q of the natural squarefree three-prime family 2pq fills a motivated class directly adjacent to an existing complete classification. Fearon et al. explicitly identify multi-prime 2-near-perfect classification as a natural problem (2025, Section 6.2). Proving there are exactly four values, including unique omitted pairs, across infinitely many eligible prime pairs is a complete natural extremal-support classification, not arbitrary cutoff enumeration. Novelty consists in the exhaustive structure, not discovering these small values; no downstream theorem is claimed.
